plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, PLTU, METU, MSFU, MUU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name limit.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by eliminating high-risk leveraged positions.
It focuses on income and broad index exposure with tighter limits.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating all leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to small allocations to reduce overall leverage.
Buy LMT at 4% as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, reducing high-beta exposure while adding a quality long setup.
It aims for a more stable growth path with a smaller cash buffer.
balanced.read: The balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month growth by reducing overall leverage and diversifying slightly. It maintains some exposure to quality tech while adding a strong new long setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Add to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to increase growth potential.
Buy LMT at 6% as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan aggressively leans into leveraged positions and high-scoring setups.
It aims for higher growth but comes with significantly increased risk and potential for larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by increasing exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring scanner setups. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Be aware of daily decay/rebalancing in leveraged ETFs and the potential for rapid losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged single names (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
It aims to park cash for yield, focusing on income-generating ETFs and broad index exposure.
income.read: The income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on steady monthly distributions and capital preservation. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
